newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Airlines weigh 3rd cargo rate rise for HK-Europe.
newsitem.headline: Airlines weigh 3rd cargo rate rise for HK-Europe.

text.p: Air cargo rates on Hong Kong to European routes may be raised for the third time in as many months to try and compensate for higher jet fuel prices, industry sources said told Reuters.

A meeting of cargo managers from the major carriers operating to Europe from Hong Kong will be held on October 2 and, if a rise is agreed, implemented on October 10, says Philippe Bour, cargo manager for Air France in Hong Kong.

Ex-Hong Kong air cargo rates to Europe are already being increased by HK$2 a kg on October 1. That rise follows a HK$3 a kg rise on August 1 by airlines complaining of a 30-40 percent reduction in rates over the past year which has badly hit yields.
Bour says airlines are also being badly affected by rising fuel prices. Jet fuel prices are reported to have increased 18 per cent so far this year in Singapore which is regarded as the bench mark.
Peter Hansen, Hong Kong-based vice-president Asia for cargo airline Polar Air said higher fuel prices were mopping up recent rises in rates.
"We're not gaining anything because we are paying more for fuel now than we ever did before," Hansen said
Philippe Bour sympathised but voiced doubts whether the market would swallow a second rate rise in 10 days.

"Some airlines are totally against it, some are reacting very slowly. As far as Air France is concerned, I'm not toally in favour of another rise. We have to do something about the fuel increase but the next meeting will decide," Bour said.
"We have to be careful about overdoing it," Bour admitted.
"I really don't know how much a rate rise would be. We are talking about HK$2 once again but I have the feeling that it will be too much to have two rate rises so close to one another," he added.
Demand currently exceeds supply in a bouyant market for European bound air cargo and some airlines are thought to be keen to take advantage.

But some Asian carriers who have a share of Hong Kong-Europe traffic via their regional hubs are said by observers to be uneasy about forcing through another rise and will urge caution at this week's meeting. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
